item.title: Incarico post-doc: Gathering the Landscape. Building a Corpus of Representations of Italy in Spanish Texts of the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Centuries (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/SPAN-01 Lingue, letterature e culture spagnola e ispano-americane

The research will focus on building SAIL’s textual corpus for its first historical phase, through a survey of Spanish texts representing the Italian landscape between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries and spanning different textual genres (memoirs, autobiographies, correspondence, as well as pre-periodical), based on archival research in Spanish and Italian institutions. The analysis of selected case studies will also contribute to an initial mapping of the places represented, recurring motifs, and representational techniques, with a view to defining the expressive ‘code’ of landscape representation.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Plato’s poets: the philosophical use of poetic references (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/HELL-01 Lingua e letteratura greca

PlatRef aims to carry out a thorough study of Plato’s strategies of poetic references and their relevance to his philosophical investigations. Extracts from poetry are found at key junctures, when new arguments or monologues are introduced. A full study of Plato’s strategies of references to poetry will open new horizons in Platonic scholarship: Plato’s multifaceted use of poetry suggest that Plato’s prose served as a vehicle to reach audiences well outside the Academy, thus questioning the educative role traditionally ascribed to poetry.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Literary Production and Scientific-Erudite Tradition in Rome Between the Late Republic and the Imperial Age (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-24 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/LATI-01 Lingua e letteratura latina

This research is aimed at studying the relationships between literary production and authors of the scientific-erudite tradition in Rome during the period between the late Republic and the Imperial age. Particular attention is given to the ways in which poets and prose writers presuppose data and concepts developed by such authors, who, for their part, also work on literary texts (often canonical or otherwise considered exemplary), aware of their own ability to determine their reception and, more generally, to influence the themes and forms of literary production, in an integrated process that is characteristic of Hellenistic-Roman culture.

This must have reflected a strong political ambition and a consensus amongst Palmyra’s most prominent citizens, and may well have provided Zenobia with the appropriate high-ranking social background to assume the role she did. The research project carries out the first mapping and comparative analysis of the "World War I Letters" collection at the Regional Archives of Cluj-Napoca, Romania (SJAN – Cluj). This little-known collection contains 557 files with letters, postcards, and war diaries (1914–1918) by Austro-Hungarian soldiers and their families. The study focuses on two main groups: Romanian common soldiers, who mostly wrote in verse following traditional oral poetry styles, and Italian soldiers from the Habsburg borderlands (Trentino, Veneto, Friuli, Venezia Giulia, Dalmatia) serving in the same army and often on the same fronts. This research proposal stems from a critical observation conducted in the urban context of Palermo: the presence of numerous ruins and sites marked by the 1943 bombings is today perceived in a distorted way by the local community and by visitors. During an observation experience at the University Language Centre (CLA), it emerged that even long-term foreign residents interpret the architectural "wounds" of the historic center as signs of mere building neglect, ignoring their wartime origin. Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/COMP-01 Comparatistica e teoria della letteratura

This research project focuses on the apparent opacity of landscapes in relation to narrative. This resistance seems to be due, on the one hand, to the lack of attention that human history has always paid to the environment, and on the other, to the gaps in the available narrative forms, which are mostly oriented towards the human scale and the immediatepresent. Consequently, these have not been sufficient to capture the complexity of places where geological, ecological and historical time are layered without ever resulting in a linear narrative
